The Warren

The Warren is the fixed Rattkin settlement beneath Calveno, built into the old drainage channels below the Le Paludi / Saltmarsh district. Calveno grew above it. The Rattkin were already there.

Rattkin origin point for the Passage. The network formed out of the Warren in 1240 DR to evade colonial pressure from the Tessarine Concordat and Dravosi Crown. Brown-rat work defines much of the Warren’s physical logic: tunnels, Holds, subsurface routes, and maps of harbour construction before outsiders know those spaces have become routes.

The Black-Jaw Run anchors the Warren in Calveno. The Tangle’s most sensitive routing intelligence sits here.

Most Dry know the Warren as rumour. Kin speak of it with more precision and less decoration — it is home, anchor, and warning all at once. Access is not obtained by asking. A person may be shown a door and still know almost nothing about what lies past it.

Physical Character

Low stone corridors and dry chambers cut into the old marsh channels, with rope bridges over flooded sections and oil lamps set into wall niches. The ceilings are low enough that most humans feel the place in their shoulders. The air smells of old stone, standing water, lamp oil, and the warmth of people living where water was supposed to go.

The sound of Calveno filters down through disguised vents: faint voices, water traffic, market noise, footsteps above. The city is always overhead, but never fully present.

The Rattle

The Warren’s alarm system. When Dravosi enter Le Paludi, someone begins striking a pan in a steady rhythm — faster when contact is close. Another household answers. Then another, then the Low Lamp, then hidden kitchens, pipes, vents. The sound travels through old stone, drainage tunnels, and cistern walls until it seems to come from everywhere at once.

To Kin, the meaning is clear: Dravosi are here. Those who cannot fight hide and lock their doors. Those who can fight answer the call. Subterfuge, sabotage, ambushes, improvised incendiaries — the Warren uses everything available when the odds are asymmetrical.

To the Dravosi, the Rattle is maddening. No one is brandishing a weapon. No one is technically obstructing an officer. No one can be arrested for washing pans or repairing cookware in a crowded district full of kitchens and canal workers. But every Crown officer feels it: surrounded, watched, counted, tracked.

Two quick taps after the Rattle stops means the threat has been dealt with.

Current Hooks

  • The Warren usually knows what is moving through Calveno before the people moving it do.
  • Do not mark a suspected entrance, boast about being invited, or mistake a rumour for permission.
  • The collector tunnels below the Warren now host Grung blackpowder magazines — Nona suspects something is building but does not know the full scope.
